# All critical covers: the adaptive game and the cost of freezing multipliers
exact geometric calibration of its quantifiers. It is not an OC bound.
The geometric example is a local minimum in an explicitly restricted
one-parameter class, and its depth is ABOVE the OC target.

The universal circuit condition and its rank consequence were already
proved in candidate a0fdd477aa859374 and
robust-circuit-gradient-rank-lemma.md. They are not claimed anew.
The additional conclusions here are:

1. an exact value for the game obtained by freezing base multipliers
   before choosing the cover;
2. a necessary and sufficient singleton criterion for that stronger
   common-multiplier property;
3. a quantitative positive gap despite universal coverwise balancing,
   realized by regular critical ambient caps of an actual family;
4. a normalized finite branch model showing that common erosion and
   homothety do not repair the allocation-quantifier swap.

## 1. The correctly ordered finite-dimensional condition

Let E be a finite-dimensional real vector space of SIGNED admissible
body-variation parameters. Fix a norm on E and its dual norm on E*.
For each deepest base p in a finite nonempty set I, let Gamma_p be
a nonempty compact convex subset of E*. In the regular critical-cap
application, Gamma_p is the closed convex hull of all normalized
critical-circuit response functionals

    L_(p,C)-beta M'.

Here L_(p,C) uses the reciprocal-section weights rho_j/S_j from
the exact quantile-cover theorem. If only a finite menu of circuits
is used, Gamma_p is a polytope and all subsequent statements are
finite linear-algebra statements.

The archived necessary condition at a local depth minimum is

    for every selection g_p in Gamma_p,
        there exists pi in the probability simplex on I
        with sum_p pi_p g_p=0.                         (U)

The order of these quantifiers is essential. Equivalently,

    Phi(v):=max_p min_(g in Gamma_p) g(v)>=0
                 for every v in E.                   (1)

Indeed failure of (U) separates one selected convex hull from zero
by a direction making all its selected functionals negative.
Conversely if (1) fails, compactness selects one negative minimizer
from each Gamma_p. This is the archived rainbow argument.

For completeness, convexifying circuit menus is legitimate: if a
convexified selected functional is negative in one direction, at
least one original functional in that convex combination is
negative. Closing the convex hull preserves strict separations.
No assertion about infinite-dimensional compactness of ALL circuit
gradients is needed; the conclusions below apply to each finite
menu in each fixed finite parameter space.

Thus the genuine sequence is: a body direction is given, a base
can protect against it, and EVERY circuit at that protecting base
has nonnegative response. The protecting base can depend on the
direction. Equivalently the balancing weights in (U) can depend
on the entire selected cover.

## 2. Exact game value with multipliers frozen in advance

Define the stronger game value

    V_fixed=max_(pi in Delta_I) min_(||v||<=1)
                      sum_p pi_p min_(g in Gamma_p) g(v).        (2)

The weight vector pi is now chosen BEFORE the direction and before
the circuit choices. Put

    R=min_(pi in Delta_I)
          max_(g_p in Gamma_p)
                      ||sum_p pi_p g_p||_*.                     (3)

All extrema in (2)--(3) are attained. In particular the function
of pi in (3) is continuous: the objective is continuous on the
product of the compact simplex and the compact circuit sets,
uniformly in those circuit choices.

**Theorem 1.**

    V_fixed=-R.                                                (4)

Moreover R=0 if and only if there is a probability vector pi
such that every Gamma_p with pi_p>0 is a singleton, say {a_p},
and sum_p pi_p a_p=0.

**Proof.** For fixed pi, nonnegativity of its coordinates and
independence of circuit choices give

    sum_p pi_p min_(g in Gamma_p)g(v)
       =min_(g_p in Gamma_p) (sum_p pi_p g_p)(v).

The two minima, over v and over the circuit product, commute.
The minimum of a linear functional a on the unit ball is
-||a||_*. Therefore the inner minimum in (2) is

    -max_(g_p in Gamma_p)||sum_p pi_p g_p||_*.

Maximizing over pi proves (4); no unjustified max-min exchange
is used.

If R=0, its attained minimizing pi satisfies

    sum_p pi_p Gamma_p={0},                                  (5)

where the left side is the Minkowski sum of sets of functionals.
Fix choices in every set except Gamma_p. If pi_p>0, subtracting
the two identities obtained from any g,g' in Gamma_p gives
pi_p(g-g')=0. Thus Gamma_p is a singleton. The selected singleton
values balance. Conversely such singleton values make (5)
hold and yield R=0.

This theorem precisely describes what freezing the multipliers
would demand: every base receiving positive weight must have
no variation at all among its circuit gradients on E. The
universal coverwise condition (U) does not demand this.

### A quantitative lower bound from circuit spread

Write D_p=diam_(||.||_*) Gamma_p. For each fixed pi,
the set sum_p pi_p Gamma_p has diameter at least pi_p D_p,
by varying just its pth entry. Its maximal norm is at least
half that diameter. Consequently, if every D_p>0,

    R >= 1 / [2 sum_p D_p^(-1)] > 0.                    (6)

Indeed max_p pi_p D_p is at least 1/sum_p D_p^(-1):
otherwise summing pi_p<(max_q pi_q D_q)/D_p gives a
contradiction. This proves (6).

The value R measures unavoidable dependence of the balancing
weights on the selected cover, in the chosen parameter norm.
It is not a lower bound for halfspace depth.

## 3. Smallest exact obstruction

Take E=R and

    Gamma_0=[a-r,a+r],       Gamma_1=[-a-r,-a+r],
    a>r>0.

Every g_0 is positive and every g_1 negative, so EVERY cover
selection balances:

    pi_0=-g_1/(g_0-g_1),   pi_1=g_0/(g_0-g_1).

Both coefficients are positive and sum to one. Thus (U) holds.
In fact

    Phi(v)=(a-r)|v|.

For fixed pi_0=t, the Minkowski sum in (5) is the interval

    [a(2t-1)-r, a(2t-1)+r].

Its maximum absolute value is |a(2t-1)|+r, minimized at t=1/2.
Therefore

    R=r,        V_fixed=-r.                            (7)

Universal balancing can thus coexist with a strictly negative
frozen-multiplier game. Scaling the functionals scales this
gap without changing the quantifier pattern.

The previously proved rank theorem is consistent with this:
the essential block has two colors and rank one. Its
low-dimensional dependence need not have fixed coefficients.

## 4. An actual complete-base family realizing the obstruction

We now realize a finite menu with a=4 and r=1/6 by actual
critical circuits of a mixed-integer body, rather than merely
by abstract vectors.

For |t|<1 define the planar trapezoid

    K_t={-1<=x<=1, -1<=y<=1+t x}.

Its area is four. Let its two scaled copies be

    A_t=(1+t)K_t,       B_t=(1-t)K_t,
    C_t=conv(({0} times A_t) union ({1} times B_t)).

C_t is a full-dimensional compact convex body in R times R^2.
Its projection is [0,1], so its actual complete integer base is
exactly {0,1}; its two integer fibers are exactly A_t,B_t.
The total mixed area is

    M_t=4(1+t)^2+4(1-t)^2=8(1+t^2).                    (8)

### Exact all-halfspace depth identity

For ANY pair of bounded fibers at the two bases 0,1, the raw
mixed depth of a point in one fiber equals its ordinary raw
depth in that fiber. One inequality holds because any ambient
cap containing the point contains an own-fiber cap through it.
For the other, any own-fiber halfspace can be extended with a
sufficiently large integer tilt to exclude the entire other
bounded fiber. Its own-fiber trace is unchanged. This applies
to every candidate and every cap orientation, including closed
boundaries.

Writing D(K_t) for the ordinary normalized maximum depth, scaling
therefore gives the exact mixed maximum

    D_MI(C_t)
       = [(1+|t|)^2/(2(1+t^2))] D(K_t).               (9)

At t=0, K_0 is the centrally symmetric square and D(K_0)=1/2.
Its center has depth 1/2 by symmetry. No point can exceed 1/2,
since opposite caps through a point split the area with null
boundary. Hence D_MI(C_0)=1/4.

### A genuine restricted local minimum

The part of K_0 removed in K_t has area |t|/2: integrate
|t x| over the half of [-1,1] where t x<0. Every square cap
containing zero has area at least two. Thus every corresponding
K_t cap has area at least 2-|t|/2, and zero still belongs to
the interior of K_t. Consequently

    D(K_t)>=1/2-|t|/8.

With s=|t|, (9) yields

    D_MI(C_t)-1/4
       >= s(7-2s-s^2)/[16(1+s^2)] > 0
                                       for 0<s<1.    (10)

Thus t=0 is a strict local minimum in this explicit SIGNED
one-parameter family. This does not assert an unrestricted
local minimum: other shape deformations are available.
Its value 1/4 is above the OC target gamma_2/2=2/9.

## 5. Actual regular critical circuits and their exact gradients

In either original square use the two opposite three-cap circuits

    C_+: x>=0, y>=0, x+y<=0;
    C_-: x<=0, y<=0, x+y>=0.                           (11)

Their unit normals have positive circuit weights (1,1,sqrt(2)).
Their own-fiber section lengths are (2,2,2sqrt(2)).
Thus the normalized reciprocal-section probabilities are
exactly (1/3,1/3,1/3).

Each cap in (11) is extended to an ambient cap excluding the
other layer strictly. For a continuous unit normal u and anchor
p in {0,1}, use

    u.X-10(1-2p)(z-p)>=0.                              (12)

At the anchor its trace is the original cap. At the other
integer layer, the constant penalty is ten, exceeding the
continuous support of both fibers for all sufficiently small
|t|. These are actual finite oblique ambient halfspaces.
At t=0 every one has mixed area two, passes through its own
maximizing center, and is critical for the raw maximum Q=2.
Each selected triple covers its entire anchor plane, as its
weighted continuous margins sum to zero there.

For K_t alone, the first two positive cap areas are

    |K_t intersect {x>=0}|=2+t/2,
    |K_t intersect {y>=0}|=2.

The negative diagonal cap has area

    2                      when t<=0,
    2-t^2/[2(1+t)]         when t>=0.                 (13)

To verify (13), its moving top intersection is
x=-1/(1+t). For t>0 the lost corner triangle has the displayed
area; for t<=0 the diagonal lies below the top throughout its
relevant x-range. Hence its derivative at zero is zero.
The opposite cap derivatives are (-1/2,0,0), since opposite
cap areas add to the constant area four.

The two circuit raw-budget derivatives in K_t are therefore
1/6 and -1/6. The caps are regular for this calculation:
the diagonal passes through two vertices but coincides with
no positive-length facet; all threshold section areas are
positive and continuous at the original cuts.

Scaling by 1+t adds four to the raw derivative of each
half-area cap; scaling by 1-t subtracts four. Because M'_0=0,
the volume-normalized raw circuit responses are

    Gamma_0=conv{4-1/6,4+1/6},
    Gamma_1=conv{-4-1/6,-4+1/6}.                        (14)

Here Gamma denotes precisely these finite circuit menus; other
critical circuits need not be classified. Exact quantile
threshold adjustments give the circuit response by the
reciprocal-section formula, so it is not necessary to assume
that the three fixed caps themselves keep equal masses after
t changes.

Equations (7) and (14) give

    R=1/6,       V_fixed=-1/6.                         (15)

For normalized depth derivative these values are divided by
M_0=8, giving -1/48 for the frozen game. Every one of the four
actual menu selections has a positive balancing probability;
no one probability vector balances all four. A common
certificate for ALL critical selections would in particular
have to handle these four, so it fails already on this menu.

This supplies an actual geometric calibration of the logical
distinction. It does not show that the full unrestricted
normal-bundle certificates at an OC counterexample behave
this way, nor does it obstruct an argument using the
below-target assumption.

## 6. Inside-allocation quantifiers and common normalization

There is a similarly exact finite model for the allocation
quantifier. It also shows why common erosion and signed
homothety, by themselves, do not permit the swap.

For parameters (s,x) near (0,0), set

    M(s,x)=2 exp(s),
    F_0(s,x)=exp(s)[1+min(x,2x)],
    F_1(s,x)=exp(s)[1+min(-x,-2x)].

These are positive near the origin and

    max(F_0,F_1)/M=(1+|x|)/2.

Thus the origin is a local minimum modulo the common scale s.
At the origin both budgets equal Q=1 and beta=1/2.
Every prescribed linear majorant of the two inside-type
minimum branches yields gradients

    g_0=(1,a),     g_1=(1,-b),      a,b in [1,2].

The objective gradient is L_0=(2,0). For EVERY a,b there
is a normalized positive certificate

    lambda_0=2b/(a+b),     lambda_1=2a/(a+b),
    L_0=lambda_0 g_0+lambda_1 g_1,
    lambda_0+lambda_1=2=1/beta.                         (16)

The signed scale direction h=(1,0) has g_j(h)=1 and
L_0(h)=2. Common erosion e=(-1,0) has g_j(e)=-1 and
L_0(e)=-2, uniformly over every prescribed allocation.
Nevertheless no single lambda handles all a,b: holding b
fixed and changing a forces lambda_0=0, incompatible with
(16) and the x-coordinate equation.

This is a finite first-order budget model, not a claim that
these two functions are realized as critical caps of an
actual mixed-integer body. In particular it does not bypass
the separate geometric zonoid restrictions on real facet
coincidences. Its exact purpose is logical: compactness,
normalization, and strict erosion alone cannot convert

    for every prescribed inside allocation,
          there exists a normalized certificate

into a certificate common to all allocations.

## 7. What remains legitimately available

The all-cover condition (U) is stronger than one-cover
stationarity, as the archived alternative-cover examples
show. But its natural finite-dimensional game is adaptive.
One cannot replace it by (2) with nonnegative value unless
one proves the extra singleton/balancing conclusion of
Theorem 1 on the relevant signed parameter space.

For a one-sided admissible cone D the corresponding common
weight requirement is

    sum_p pi_p Gamma_p subset D^+,
    D^+={ell:ell(v)>=0 for every v in D}.

It need not force singleton sets; the stronger conclusion
above uses SIGNED directions. This distinction prevents
applying the singleton test to the Green cone without first
restricting to its lineality.

Likewise, the full normal-bundle theorem has the order
forall cover, forall inside allocation, exists multipliers
and outside allocations satisfying every body test.
Our finite theorem does not change that order and does not
claim that one boundary source must work for all covers.
A common source could conceivably admit different cap
representations; freezing base weights is a separate,
strictly stronger condition. Any such source-intersection
theorem would require additional geometric input.
